title: Vector spaces, subspaces, Nul A, Col A, kernel & range
summary: Vector spaces generalize ℝⁿ to polynomials, matrices and functions. The subspace test, and the two subspaces attached to every matrix (Nul A in ℝⁿ, Col A in ℝᵐ) and to every linear map (kernel and range), are tested on every final.

blocks.text: A nonempty set V of objects (vectors) with an addition and a scalar multiplication satisfying ten axioms: closure under both operations, commutativity and associativity of +, a zero vector 0, additive inverses −u, distributive laws c(u + v) = cu + cv and (c + d)u = cu + du, c(du) = (cd)u, and 1u = u.

items: ℝⁿ: column vectors.
ℙₙ: polynomials of degree at most n, a₀ + a₁t + ⋯ + aₙtⁿ (the zero polynomial included).
Mₘₓₙ: m×n matrices.
C[a, b] or C(ℝ): continuous functions; the zero vector is the zero function.
The space of all real functions on a set, or all solutions of a homogeneous linear ODE.

blocks.text: The point of the abstraction: everything we proved about ℝⁿ using only + and scalar multiplication (spans, independence, linear maps, kernels) works verbatim for polynomials, matrices and functions.
A subset H of a vector space V such that (a) 0 ∈ H; (b) u, v ∈ H ⇒ u + v ∈ H; (c) u ∈ H, c scalar ⇒ cu ∈ H. A subspace is itself a vector space.

blocks.name: Spans are subspaces
blocks.text: For any v₁, …, vₚ in V, Span{v₁, …, vₚ} is a subspace of V.

proof.text: 0 = 0v₁ + ⋯ + 0vₚ; the sum of two combinations is a combination; a multiple of a combination is a combination.

blocks.title: How to answer 'is H a subspace?'
items: Check 0 ∈ H first: if not, stop, the answer is no.
If yes, try to write H as a span or as the kernel (solution set of a homogeneous linear condition) of a linear map: then it is a subspace.
Otherwise look for an explicit failure of closure: two specific members whose sum is not in H, or a member and a scalar.

blocks.title: A polynomial set that fails
blocks.prompt: Is H = {p ∈ ℙ₂ : p(1) = 1} a subspace of ℙ₂? What about K = {p ∈ ℙ₂ : p(1) = 0}?
steps: H: the zero polynomial has value 0 at t = 1, not 1. So 0 ∉ H: condition (a) fails.
(Closure fails too: p = 1 and q = t are in H but (p + q)(1) = 2; and 2p has 2p(1) = 2.)
Better: K is the kernel of the linear map p ↦ p(1), so it is a subspace automatically. Basis: {t − 1, t² − 1}.
blocks.answer: H is not a subspace (no zero vector, not closed); K is a subspace.

blocks.title: Matrix and ℝ³ sets
blocks.prompt: Which are subspaces? (a) {A ∈ M₂ₓ₂ : det A = 0}. (b) {A ∈ M₂ₓ₂ : A = Aᵀ}. (c) {(x, y, z) : x + 2y = z}. (d) {(x, y, z) : xy = 0}.
steps: (a) No: [1 0; 0 0] and [0 0; 0 1] have det 0 but their sum I has det 1.
(c) Yes: the null space of [1 2 −1].
(d) No: (1, 0, 0) and (0, 1, 0) are in it, (1, 1, 0) is not (a union of two planes).
blocks.answer: (b) and (c) are subspaces; (a) and (d) are not.

blocks.text: Nonlinear conditions (det = 0, xy = 0, x² + y² ≤ 1, x ≥ 0) almost never give subspaces. Unions of subspaces are usually not subspaces; intersections always are.
Nul A = {x ∈ ℝⁿ : Ax = 0} for an m×n matrix A. A subspace of ℝⁿ (n = number of columns). Implicitly defined: membership is easy to check, but you must solve to list elements.
{x : Ax = b} with b ≠ 0 is NEVER a subspace: 0 is not in it (A0 = 0 ≠ b), and the sum of two solutions solves Ax = 2b. It is a translate p + Nul A.
Col A = Span{columns of A} = {Ax : x ∈ ℝⁿ} = {b : Ax = b is consistent}. A subspace of ℝᵐ (m = number of rows). Explicitly defined: easy to list elements, but membership requires row reduction.

blocks.name: Col A = ℝᵐ
blocks.text: Col A = ℝᵐ ⇔ Ax = b is consistent for every b ⇔ pivot in every row.

blocks.title: Bases for Nul A and Col A
items: Row reduce A to RREF.
Nul A: solve Ax = 0 in parametric vector form; the vectors multiplying the free variables form a basis (one per free variable).
Col A: identify the pivot columns from the echelon form, then take those columns of the ORIGINAL A.

blocks.title: Bases for Nul A and Col A
blocks.prompt: A = [−3 6 −1 1 −7; 1 −2 2 3 −1; 2 −4 5 8 −4]. Find bases for Nul A and Col A, and describe Col A by an equation.
steps: RREF(A) = [1 −2 0 −1 3; 0 0 1 2 −2; 0 0 0 0 0]. Pivots in columns 1 and 3; x₂, x₄, x₅ free.
x₁ = 2x₂ + x₄ − 3x₅, x₃ = −2x₄ + 2x₅.
Col A basis: columns 1 and 3 of A: (−3, 1, 2) and (−1, 2, 5).
Col A is a plane in ℝ³ with normal (−3, 1, 2) × (−1, 2, 5) = (1, 13, −5): b₁ + 13b₂ − 5b₃ = 0.

blocks.text: Row operations change the column space. The pivot columns of RREF(A) here are e₁, e₂, which are not even in Col A (check: 1 + 0 − 0 ≠ 0).

blocks.title: Membership in Nul A and Col A
blocks.prompt: For the same A: is u = (3, 1, −2, 1, 0) in Nul A? Is (1, 1, 1, 0, −1)? Is (2, 1, 3) in Col A? Is (1, 0, 0)?
steps: Col A: test the consistency condition b₁ + 13b₂ − 5b₃ = 0 (or row reduce [A | b]). (2, 1, 3): 2 + 13 − 15 = 0, yes.

lesson.title: Row space and comparing Nul A with Col A

blocks.text: Row A = Span{rows of A} = Col Aᵀ, a subspace of ℝⁿ.

blocks.name: Row operations preserve the row space
blocks.text: If B is row equivalent to A, Row B = Row A. The nonzero rows of an echelon form of A are a basis of Row A.

proof.text: Each new row is a combination of old rows and vice versa (operations are reversible).

lesson.title: Linear transformations between vector spaces: kernel and range

blocks.text: T: V → W with T(u + v) = T(u) + T(v) and T(cu) = cT(u).
Ker T = {u ∈ V : T(u) = 0}, a subspace of V. Range T = {T(u) : u ∈ V}, a subspace of W. For T(x) = Ax: Ker T = Nul A and Range T = Col A.

blocks.title: Kernel and range of a map on ℙₙ or matrices
items: Check linearity using linearity of evaluation, differentiation, transpose or integration.
Write a general input (a + bt + ct², or [a b; c d]) and compute T of it.
Kernel: set the output to zero and solve for the coefficients.
Range: the span of the images of a basis; simplify to a basis. Check: dim Ker + dim Range = dim V.

blocks.title: Kernel and range of p ↦ (p(0), p(1))
blocks.prompt: T: ℙ₂ → ℝ², T(p) = (p(0), p(1)). Show T is linear; find its kernel and range.
steps: Linear: (p + q)(0) = p(0) + q(0), (cp)(0) = c·p(0), and the same at 1.
For p = a + bt + ct²: T(p) = (a, a + b + c). (Matrix relative to {1, t, t²}: [1 0 0; 1 1 1].)
Kernel: a = 0 and a + b + c = 0 ⇒ c = −b. p = b(t − t²). Ker T = Span{t − t²} (the polynomials vanishing at 0 and 1: multiples of t(t − 1)).
Range: T(1) = (1, 1), T(t) = (0, 1) are independent, so the range is all of ℝ²: T is onto.
Check: dim Ker + dim Range = 1 + 2 = 3 = dim ℙ₂.
blocks.answer: Ker T = Span{t − t²}; Range T = ℝ² (onto).

blocks.title: Linear or not?
blocks.prompt: Which are linear? (a) T: ℙ₂ → ℙ₂, T(p) = p + 1. (b) T: M₂ₓ₂ → ℝ, T(A) = trace A. (c) T: ℙ₂ → ℝ, T(p) = p(0)·p(1).
steps: (a) Not linear: T(0) = 1 ≠ 0.
(b) Linear: tr(A + B) = tr A + tr B, tr(cA) = c tr A. Kernel = trace-zero matrices (dimension 3).
(c) Not linear: T(2p) = 4T(p), e.g. p = 1 gives T(2) = 4 ≠ 2 = 2T(1).

blocks.title: Six True/False
blocks.prompt: (a) Nul A is the set of all linear combinations of the columns of A. (b) If A is 3×5, Nul A is a subspace of ℝ³. (c) The intersection of two subspaces is a subspace. (d) The union of two subspaces is a subspace. (e) Col A is the set of all b for which Ax = b has a solution. (f) The kernel of a linear map is a subspace of the codomain.
steps: (a) False: that is Col A.
(b) False: Nul A ⊆ ℝ⁵ (number of columns).
(c) True: closure in each gives closure in both.
(d) False: x-axis ∪ y-axis contains e₁, e₂ but not e₁ + e₂.
(e) True.
(f) False: it is a subspace of the domain.
blocks.answer: (a) F (b) F (c) T (d) F (e) T (f) F

blocks.text: Remember: Nul A ↔ inputs ↔ ℝⁿ ↔ uniqueness. Col A ↔ outputs ↔ ℝᵐ ↔ existence.

cards.front: Three conditions for a subspace H of V?

back.text: 0 ∈ H; closed under addition; closed under scalar multiplication.

cards.front: Fastest way to prove a set IS a subspace?

back.text: Show it is a span, or the kernel / null space of a linear map (solutions of a homogeneous linear condition).

cards.front: Fastest way to prove a set is NOT a subspace?

back.text: Show 0 is missing; otherwise give two specific elements whose sum (or a scalar multiple) leaves the set.

cards.front: Is {p ∈ ℙ₂ : p(1) = 1} a subspace?

back.text: No: the zero polynomial has p(1) = 0 ≠ 1 (and closure fails: (p + q)(1) = 2).

cards.front: Why is Nul A always a subspace but {x : Ax = b}, b ≠ 0, never?

back.text: A0 = 0 and A is linear, so solutions of Ax = 0 are closed. For b ≠ 0, A0 = 0 ≠ b, so 0 is missing; the set is p + Nul A.

cards.front: Is ℝ² a subspace of ℝ³?

back.text: No: it is not even a subset. The plane {(x, y, 0)} is a subspace that looks like ℝ².

cards.front: Nul A: definition and where it lives?

back.text: {x : Ax = 0} ⊆ ℝⁿ (n = number of columns). Implicit description.

cards.front: Col A: definition and where it lives?

back.text: Span of the columns = {Ax} = {b : Ax = b consistent} ⊆ ℝᵐ (m = number of rows). Explicit description.

cards.front: Basis for Nul A?

back.text: RREF, parametric vector form of Ax = 0; the vectors multiplying the free variables. Count = number of free variables.

cards.front: Basis for Col A?

back.text: The pivot columns of the ORIGINAL A (row operations change the column space).

cards.front: Basis for Row A?

back.text: The nonzero rows of an echelon form of A (row operations preserve the row space).

cards.front: Which of Nul A, Col A, Row A do row operations preserve?

back.text: Nul A and Row A. Not Col A.

cards.front: Test whether v ∈ Nul A; whether v ∈ Col A.

back.text: Nul: compute Av and see if it is 0. Col: row reduce [A | v] and check consistency.

cards.front: Kernel and range of linear T: V → W?

back.text: Ker T = {u : T(u) = 0} ⊆ V; Range T = {T(u)} ⊆ W. For T(x) = Ax they are Nul A and Col A.

cards.front: Kernel of T: ℙ₂ → ℝ², p ↦ (p(0), p(1))?

back.text: Span{t − t²} (polynomials with roots 0 and 1); the range is ℝ².

cards.front: Is the union of two subspaces a subspace? The intersection?

back.text: Union: usually not (x-axis ∪ y-axis). Intersection: always.

cards.front: Solutions of y″ + p(t)y′ + q(t)y = 0: a subspace?

back.text: Yes: the kernel of the linear operator L[y] = y″ + py′ + qy. With a nonzero forcing g, no (0 is not a solution); they form yₚ + Ker L.

cards.front: Is {A ∈ M₂ₓ₂ : det A = 0} a subspace?
Is T(p) = p + 1 linear on ℙ₂?
Col A = ℝᵐ iff?

back.text: Pivot in every row (Ax = b consistent for every b).

prompt.text: Decide which of these are subspaces. Give a proof or a specific failure.

items: 1. {p ∈ ℙ₃ : p(2) = 0} is a subspace of ℙ₃.
2. {p ∈ ℙ₃ : p(0) = 1} is a subspace of ℙ₃.
3. {A ∈ M₂ₓ₂ : det A = 0} is a subspace.
4. {f ∈ C[0, 1] : ∫₀¹ f(t) dt = 0} is a subspace.
5. {(x, y, z) : xy = 0} is a subspace of ℝ³.
6. For a fixed B, {A ∈ M₂ₓ₂ : AB = BA} is a subspace.
7. {f : ℝ → ℝ with f(x + 1) = 2f(x) for all x} is a subspace of the space of all functions.

solution.text: 1. True. Contains 0; (p+q)(2) = 0 + 0; (cp)(2) = 0. (It is the kernel of the linear map p ↦ p(2).)
2. False. The zero polynomial has value 0 at 0. Fails at the very first test.
are in it; their sum I has det 1. Not closed under addition.
4. True. Integration is linear, so this is the kernel of a linear map.
5. False. (1, 0, 0) and (0, 1, 0) are in it; their sum (1, 1, 0) is not. (It’s the union of two planes.)
7. True. If f, g satisfy it, (af + bg)(x+1) = 2af(x) + 2bg(x); and 0 works. (2x is a nonzero member.)

What it tests: Three checks: contains 0, closed under +, closed under scalar multiples. Fastest proof of “yes”: show it is the kernel of a linear map. Fastest “no”: 0 missing, or one explicit failing sum.

hard.title: Nul A and Col A with membership

prompt.text: (a) Nul A is a subspace of ℝ^? and Col A of ℝ^? (b) Find bases for Nul A and Col A. (c) Describe Col A by one equation. (d) Is (1, 1, 1) in Col A? Is (1, 4, 1)?

solution.text: What it tests: Col basis comes from the original matrix’s pivot columns, never from rref (rref’s columns all have last entry 0 here). Nul basis vectors = one per free variable.

items: 1. Col A is the set of all solutions of Ax = b.
2. If A is 4×6, Col A can equal ℝ⁴.
3. If A is 4×6, Nul A can be {0}.
4. A line in ℝ³ not through the origin is a subspace.
5. The union of two subspaces of V is a subspace.
6. The intersection of two subspaces of V is a subspace.
1. False. Col A is the set of all b for which Ax = b is solvable (lives in ℝᵐ); solution sets live in ℝⁿ.
2. True. E.g. [I₄ 0]. Four pivots fit in a 4×6 matrix.
3. False. At most 4 pivots ⇒ at least 2 free variables.
4. False. Doesn’t contain 0.
5. False. The x-axis ∪ the y-axis in ℝ² contains e₁ and e₂ but not e₁ + e₂.
6. True. If u, v are in both, so is any combination, since each subspace is closed.

solution.text: What it tests: Keep the two homes straight: Nul A ⊆ ℝⁿ (number of columns), Col A ⊆ ℝᵐ (number of rows).

hard.title: Kernel and range of X ↦ X − Xᵀ

prompt.text: Define T: M₂ₓ₂ → M₂ₓ₂ by T(X) = X − Xᵀ. Show T is linear and find bases for its kernel and range. Check that dimensions add up.

solution.text: What it tests: Kernel and range of maps on matrix spaces are sets of matrices. The rank theorem still applies with dim M₂ₓ₂ = 4.

hard.title: Kernel and range on ℙ₃

prompt.text: T: ℙ₃ → ℙ₃, T(p) = t·p′(t) − p(t). Find the kernel and range of T. Is t³ + 1 in the range? Is t + 1?

hard.answer: Ker = Span{t}; Range = Span{1, t², t³}; t³ + 1 yes, t + 1 no

solution.title: Solution
items: Kernel: a = c = d = 0: Span{t}. Range: Span{1, t², t³} (dim 3; 1 + 3 = 4 ✓).
t³ + 1 = T(−1 + ½t³): yes. t + 1 has a t term: no.

solution.text: What it tests: Compute T on a basis. The range is spanned by the images; the missing direction (t) is exactly why t + 1 is unreachable.

hard.title: Col A = Nul A

prompt.text: (a) Find a 2×2 matrix A with Col A = Nul A. (b) Prove no 3×3 matrix has Col A = Nul A.

hard.answer: (a) A = [0 1; 0 0] (b) rank = nullity would make 3 even

solution.text: (b) If Col A = Nul A, then rank = nullity, but rank + nullity = 3 is odd. Impossible. ∎
What it tests: Rank theorem parity trick. In general Col A = Nul A needs n even and A² = 0.

hard.title: Sum of subspaces

prompt.text: H, K are subspaces of V. Prove H + K = {h + k : h ∈ H, k ∈ K} is a subspace of V, and that it contains both H and K.

hard.answer: H + K contains 0 and is closed under + and scalars by regrouping; h = h + 0

solution.title: Solution
items: (h₁ + k₁) + (h₂ + k₂) = (h₁ + h₂) + (k₁ + k₂), with the parentheses in H and K respectively.
h = h + 0 shows H ⊆ H + K; same for K. (Unlike H ∪ K, this is a subspace — the smallest one containing both.)

solution.text: What it tests: Write general elements with names and regroup. Each step uses closure of H or K.

hard.title: Col(AB) ⊆ Col A and Nul B ⊆ Nul(AB)

prompt.text: A is m×n, B is n×p. Prove Col(AB) ⊆ Col A and Nul B ⊆ Nul(AB). Give 2×2 matrices for which both inclusions are strict.

solution.text: : AB = 0. Col(AB) = {0} ⊊ Span{e₁} = Col A; Nul B = Span{e₁} ⊊ ℝ² = Nul(AB).
What it tests: These two inclusions give rank(AB) ≤ rank A and rank(AB) ≤ rank B.

hard.title: Solution spaces of linear ODEs

prompt.text: Let p, q, g be continuous on ℝ. (a) Show the solutions of y″ + p(t)y′ + q(t)y = 0 form a subspace of C²(ℝ). (b) Show the solutions of y″ + py′ + qy = g with g ≢ 0 do not, and describe them in terms of (a). (c) Is {sin²t, cos²t, 1} linearly independent in C(ℝ)?

hard.answer: (a) kernel of the linear operator L (b) 0 is not a solution; solutions = yₚ + Ker L (c) No: sin²t + cos²t − 1 = 0

solution.title: Solution
items: (a) L[y] = y″ + py′ + qy is linear: L[ay₁ + by₂] = aL[y₁] + bL[y₂]. The solution set is Ker L, a subspace.
(b) y = 0 gives L[0] = 0 ≠ g, so 0 is not a solution. If yₚ is one solution, all solutions are yₚ + Ker L (exactly like p + Nul A).
(c) No: sin²t + cos²t − 1 = 0 for all t is a nontrivial relation.

solution.text: What it tests: Linear ODEs are linear maps on function spaces. “General solution = particular + homogeneous” is the same theorem as p + Nul A for linear systems.

keyFacts: Subspace: contains 0, closed under + and scalar multiplication. Spans and kernels are always subspaces.
Nul A = {x : Ax = 0} ⊆ ℝⁿ; Col A = span of columns = {b : Ax = b consistent} ⊆ ℝᵐ.
{x : Ax = b}, b ≠ 0, is never a subspace (no 0); it is p + Nul A.
Nul A basis: free-variable vectors from RREF. Col A basis: pivot columns of the ORIGINAL A.
Row operations preserve Nul A and Row A, not Col A.
v ∈ Nul A: check Av = 0. v ∈ Col A: row reduce [A | v].
Ker T ⊆ domain, Range T ⊆ codomain; for T(x) = Ax they are Nul A, Col A.
